scopes.headline: The biggest problem is that the personalization axes resolve only where they are set on the root. On a nested UIProvider, brand and surface half apply (P1), radius and type scale do nothing, and aqua and terminal lose their mode-split palettes. One P1 and 15 P2 findings; 2 of 10 subjects (modern, retro) are ready. The sweep and all five styles checks pass (check:tokens, check:roles, check:figma, check:dtcg, check:z-layers), but: the token-economy dead-token scan is a no-op, and 60 unread --a63-* tokens exist. Two undeclared contrast pairs fail: nested-dark status foreground at 3.39/3.85:1, and chart-2/3 against the light page at about 2.3/2.0:1. The type scale is non-monotonic (10xl < 9xl at 768px+). Tailwind spacing ignores density. Figma leaves out phone and compact control geometry, and shows terminal's brand-tracking colors as b1 only. Disclosure: one broad grep over docs/ printed a few lines from readiness-r1 JSON (r1-tokens-1/2). The nested-brand defect had already been found independently before that, and the surface-axis part was then re-verified from source.

最大问题是：contract 写的东西和实际渲染出来的对不上，而且没有检查去发现。Button 的 contract 列出的 5 个 slot 名（root、label、icon、spinner、indicator）在 DOM 里一个都没有，CLI 却把它们和真正的 data-slot="button" 放在同一个回答里给 agent（唯一的 P1）。其余 16 个 subject 中 15 个未达 ready，问题都是 P2。缺 axis 或 state：toggle-group 的 size/tone、connected-panel 的 variant、search-field 的 size/invalid、checkbox 的 hover/focus-visible、sidebar 的各个 state、sidebar-nav-tree 没有 slots 列表。一致性检查只看名为 sizes/states 的列表里的值，所以漏掉了：sidebar menuButtonSizes 用 "default"；menu 的 tone 叫 "primary"，其他组件叫 "accent"；badge 的 "accent" 其实是中性色，"neutral" 是色板色相；aligns 和 alignments 并存；slot 有三套命名方式。基线里的 5 个同义词（input/textarea/search-field 的 focus、field 的 default、load-more-trigger 的 idle）判为 P2。跨渲染器方面（只看 JSON）：badge 在 strict parity 下的 requiredStates 和自己的 intent tone 轴对不上；amount 有 iOS 对应物（AtomAmountText），但没有映射。menu 是内部 helper，却以 stable 的公开组件 contract 身份导出。只有 card 达到 ready。生成检查（contracts --check、cross-renderer --check）和 agent-index 都通过。

The biggest problem is Y1 evidence. Only list-page is captured at 768 and 1440. For every other story outside list-page, visual.setup.ts:25-32 forces the viewport to 1280, and phone width applies only when the story id ends in -phone. So AppView's Phone* stories are captured at 1280 too. I found no P0 or P1 issues and 20 P2s. Besides Y1, the P2s are: (1) safe areas: the app-view phone sample and the `atom63 build` snippet use raw env(); sign-in, Page and ReaderLayout have no inset owner. (2) Real-content stress cases are missing for activity-list empty, an all-done checklist, long page-header titles, long stat-row values and long or empty app-view lists. (3) Composition: 14 ghost buttons in the templates have no tone="muted"; list-page shows two primary buttons when there are no invoices; the sign-in card is not centred (Page min-h-full); tab-bar uses text-[0.6875rem]; AppView's default labels are 'Player' and 'Library'; Section's gap ramp is not monotonic. (4) Findability: the CLI does not lead builders to ReaderLayout. Five subjects are ready: app-shell, data-table-section, detail-panel, empty-state and filter-bar. Taste scores (Y4) are provisional until YZ checks them.

The biggest problem is that the @atom63/ui-react root entry does not tree-shake: importing only Kbd or Button costs 36-39 kB gzip and Separator 110 kB, and the total-size budget (97.3/100 kB) cannot see per-import cost (one P1). There are 15 P2s: mdx's 'lightweight' credits-block entry is 164 kB gzip and a helper-only import from widgets/state is 167 kB; there is no CSS budget (consumer CSS grew 74->81 kB gzip in two days); react-hook-form is a required peer that the root imports eagerly; mdx, widgets and inform exact-pin ui-react as a dependency, so upgrading ui-react alone installs a second copy; styles, ui-foundation and cli have no tiers, and mdx calls its beta entries 'stable'; Release beta failed twice on main with 'nothing to commit' (the fix is not merged); PR CI depends on the live npm registry; the WebKit sign-in flake is untracked. The dependency graph is one-way with no cycles, but no check enforces that. Ready: agent, templates, private tooling. iOS (K10) is out of scope this round, so this layer has no K10 score and no iOS findings.

Layer 6 (web/React): 0 of 5 subjects are ready, with 1 P1, 7 P2 and 4 P3. The P1 is U2: 7 of the 15 AGENTS.md rules name no check and give no reason, and check:agents-md only checks that the block is in sync. The CLI's core answers match the source (contracts, Amount props; MCP comes from the same command table, 17/17 tests pass). Gaps: preview APIs are answered with the root import. JS-export answers have no props. The Markdown twins drop live JSX examples (InformBanner is missing from pattern-inform.md). The starter still gives agents the docs-only AGENTS.md on the stale claim that the CLI is unpublished, and @atom63/create is private. U5 is unmeasured on current main: 28 commits since Round 13a, no rerun, and the Round 13a report is untracked.

最大问题是：8 个 actions 组件没有一个达到 ready，但全部卡在 P2（无 P0/P1）。共性缺口有三类：(1) 6 个组件的 atom63 component 文档是原型模板套话（对 Toggle/Kbd/链接写「invalid state」「explain errors」「loading/destructive」），且没有可运行示例；(2) 触控 44px 目标被 overflow 裁掉：Aqua 主题下 icon Button 的 overflow:hidden（button.css:159-161）和 ButtonGroup 的 overflow-x:auto 都会裁掉 ::before 热区，默认 CopyButton 在 Aqua+touch 只有 32px，而运行时 target-size 规则只查 24px；(3) 硬编码英文：CopyButton 的「Copied!」、错误 toast，默认 toast 会显示「Copy copied to clipboard」；DestinationLink 的「(opens in new tab)」。其他实测问题：Toggle subtle 色调只靠色相区分按下状态（两态亮度比 1.46:1）；PanelSettingButton 激活态图标在所有暗色模式下只有 2.04-2.14:1；Button loading 走原生 disabled，会让焦点掉到 body，用 render 渲染成 时禁用不住；ToggleGroup 合同里的 selectionMode 在 React API 中不存在（实际是 multiple），且窄屏没有溢出处理；KbdGroup 渲染为

里会触发 hydration 报错；Kbd 有两条 craft-baseline 欠账，而 tooltip 内的样式没有任何截图基线。K3 为暂定分，需 YZ 看 contact sheet 确认；K10 按 iOS backlog 记为 n/a。

None of the 8 batch-2 subjects is ready. The biggest problem is two P1 accessibility gaps. Rating's amber stars measure about 2.1:1 on the light page, and an on star differs from an off star only by colour. SegmentedControl uses tab roles with no tab panels, and its tablist cannot be named. One batch-wide P2 holds radio, switch and checkbox below ready: no baseline captures hover, focus-visible, pressed or dragging. Radio and switch would otherwise be ready, and checkbox would still be missing a capture of its invalid state. Spinner is the weakest subject, with six criteria at 2. K10 is n/a (iOS backlog).

最大问题是表单字段整体在触控和状态覆盖上仍未达标：10 个对象只有 label 达到 ready，没有 P0/P1，但有 18 个 P2。主要缺口：(1) 输入类控件在 web 设计语言的粗指针下仍是 32px，未达到 input.json 声明的 44px 触控目标（select.mdx 还错误地声称已有最小目标）；(2) input/textarea/search-field/input-otp/autocomplete 没有任何 focus-visible 基线，search-field 的 query 状态和 field 的 disabled 状态也未截图；(3) input 文档承诺 autofill 是设计过的状态，但仓库里没有任何 autofill CSS；(4) Field 的 invalid/disabled 没有类型化 prop，需要三处信号，FieldError 单独出现时只设 aria-invalid、不变红；(5) AutocompleteInput 绕过 --a63-field-* token，在 terminal 主题下与 Input/Select 不一致，且没有 APG 模式绑定；(6) search-field-input 这个 contract 插槽从未渲染；(7) input-otp 在 RTL 下槽位镜像，验证码会倒着显示；(8) Form 的标准示例用 aria-label 覆盖了可见标签；(9) Amount 不传 locale 时会出现 SSR hydration 不一致；(10) terminal 浅色主题里 placeholder 颜色几乎等于输入值颜色（token 层问题，标为 yz-decision）。K3 为暂定分，需 YZ 看 contact sheet 确认；K10 全部为 null（iOS backlog）。

Batch 4 overlays: 1 of 10 ready (only portal-container). There are 3 P1s, 25 P2s and 12 P3s. The biggest problem is the toaster: its default toast never takes the overlay theme tokens, and its Playground and Dark baselines capture no toast. Popover also exports PopoverAnchor, which anchors nothing. Sheet and Drawer lack aria-modal, the gap Dialog already patched. Dialog's close button is 32px on touch. Several Themes baselines are overlapped or empty (popover, hover-card, preview-card, tooltip, drawer). Dialog and alert-dialog are each one or two P2s from ready.

最大问题是 Tabs 默认样式在竖排时是坏的。原因：轨道高度固定为一行，滑动指示器也不读 --active-tab-top，竖排时不会跟着选中项移动；而且没有任何竖排的 story、截图基线或测试。第二个 P1：menu contract 标了 stable，但 `atom63 component menu` 查不到，它的 primary tone 只能靠手写 data-tone 属性用上。9 个组件都还没到 ready。P2 主要有四类：（1）粗指针下，菜单、命令面板、导航菜单、Tabs 的行高或点击区只有 32px，达不到 44px，Command 的注释还写错成 44px；（2）子菜单和分页的箭头在 RTL 下不镜像，分页的 Previous/Next 文案写死、没法本地化；（3）DropdownMenu、ContextMenu、Menubar 打开后的样子从来没截过图；（4）除 dropdown-menu 和 tabs 外，其余组件只有生成的文档页。另有几个具体缺陷：NavigationMenuIndicator 是导出了但不起作用的空壳；导航触发器的箭头按 lucide 默认的 24px 渲染，比文字大一截；⌘K 弹窗没有可访问名称；面包屑折叠后的省略号点不了，被折叠的层级到不了；分页的上一页/下一页没有禁用态。K10 全部记为 n/a（iOS 在 backlog）。

The biggest problem is the Card interactive variant: it is pointer-only and its own examples teach it (P1). Only frame of the 10 batch-6 subjects is ready. 19 P2s, mostly concrete bugs: Accordion drops its root class whenever className is passed (this hits the MDX block); the Resizable drag-state selector is a stale v2 attribute; the ScrollArea/ScrollableList fade mask fades the wrong edges in RTL (visible in the RTL baseline); Item line clamps never apply; separators vanish in forced-colors mode; ConnectedPanel content clips at narrow widths and its variant axis is not in the contract. Also: missing state baselines (accordion disabled, collapsible closed), Collapsible docs never say the trigger is unstyled, and resizable and accordion lack behaviour tests.

最大问题是 batch 7 没有一个组件 ready（0/8）：两个 P1，都在标成 stable 的组件上，按 C5 这两个组件不该标 stable。一是 Sidebar 在 RTL 下默认的桌面布局会错位，二是 TextTicker 的 autoPlay 无法暂停，不符合 WCAG 2.2.2。另有 25 个 P2，集中在四类问题：选中/当前态在 forced-colors 下消失（calendar、table、sidebar、carousel）；调用方传入的 ref 或 onClick 覆盖了内部的 ref 和 onClick（carousel、text-ticker）；触屏目标小于 44px（calendar 36px、carousel 圆点宽 24px）；视觉基线在 reduced motion 下截图，Marquee 的暂停按钮和 TextTicker 的动态状态都没被截到，TextTicker 的截图里首字被遮罩淡化。没有 P0；K10 都记为 n/a（iOS 在 backlog）。

Batch 8, feedback and status (web and React only): none of the 8 subjects is ready. 1 P1: in dark mode the LoadMoreTrigger Retry label uses --a63-action-danger, which measures about 2.8:1 against the 4.5:1 that text needs. There are also 21 P2 and 6 P3 findings. The main P2 clusters: FeedbackState, LoadMoreTrigger and Empty have API gaps (no rest props, boolean props that duplicate the state prop, a detail panel that cannot be controlled). Avatar, Badge, Empty and Skeleton have RTL or long-string gaps. The CLI answers for FeedbackState and Skeleton describe states and outcomes the components do not implement. Two findings are left for YZ: whether Avatar should carry the theme look, and whether Empty and FeedbackState should overlap. All K10 scores are null (iOS backlog).

最大问题是 message：失败状态几乎看不出来（和已送达的消息一样是主题色气泡，只多一个 12px 的图标），主题基线没有经过 ThemeMatrix，所以看不出各主题的原型差异，而且完全没有手机宽度的证据。本批 5 个里 2 个 ready（chat-steps、chat-typing-indicator），没有 P0 或 P1。另外 4 个 P2：chat-composer 按停止后焦点会丢到页面上（只读代码推断，没在浏览器里跑）；预填的长文本仍留在圆形胶囊里；chat-message 没有出错状态，但 @atom63/agent 有 'error'；message 没有手机宽度的 story。K10 按要求记为 null（n/a: iOS backlog）。

The biggest problem is the cross-package gaps, which keep 43 of 44 subjects from being ready. The four packages have no theme captures: of the 202 baselines, none is aqua, retro or terminal (K3=2). The CI ssr project renders only ui-react stories (K9=2). MDX has no phone stories (K7=2). Most MDX blocks, all inform surfaces and the widget card parts drop rest props and refs (K1=2). For inform surfaces and widgets, `atom63 api` gives no props or examples (K8=2). There is one P1: InformSpotlight's scrim and cutout are box-shadow only and vanish in forced colors. Other P2s: inform's dismiss control is 24px with no 44px coarse-pointer rule; ImageCompare's slider name is fixed English; InformDialog drops dismissLabel and its close button is hard-coded 'Close'; the flyout stack ignores safe areas; WidgetAvatar drops focus while busy and its shuffle control is invisible on touch; ResourceList uses physical left/right positioning; DocExample sizes its targets by breakpoint, not pointer; WidgetImage has no story; AppLogo takes no rest props or ref. The only ready subject is the inform runtime (InformProvider/InformOutlet), and only because K2, K3, K5 and K7 are n/a there. K10 is null throughout (iOS backlog), and K3 scores are provisional until YZ sees the contact sheets.

findings.subject: Personalization axes (brand, surface, surface tint, radius, type scale, density, font, mode)
findings.summary: On a nested scope, the brand and surface axes only half apply. <UIProvider brand=...> or <UIProvider surface=...> without a mode changes the primary fill but leaves links, the focus ring, the accent selection, the choice-card check and every surface, text and border token on the root's brand and neutrals.
findings.evidence: provider.tsx:68,73 stamp data-a63-brand or data-a63-surface alone. brand-action.css:14-15 re-declares only the primary action on [data-a63-brand]. --a63-text-accent (semantics.css:161,360), --a63-focus-ring (:209,395), --a63-selected-accent-background (:301,445), --a63-choice-card-checked-* (:199-205,388-393) and the surfaces and borders that read --surface-light/dark-* and --a63-brand-* (:100-185, :307-379) are declared only on ':root, .light, [data-a63-mode]' and ':is(.dark,[data-a63-mode=dark])', so they resolve at the ancestor and inherit frozen values. personalization-axes.md:4 promises 'applied at any scope'; :71 wrongly places --a63-focus-ring in brand.css on [data-a63-brand]. The nested-scope tests stamp theme and mode together (contrast.browser.test.ts:189-191), and the brand tests use the root only (:237). Stories always pass mode with brand (button.stories.tsx:692, switch.stories.tsx:327), which hides the bug.
findings.fix: Add [data-a63-brand] and [data-a63-surface] to the selector lists of both mode blocks of semantics.css, keyed to the inherited mode. The simplest form is to generate the light block as ':root, .light, [data-a63-mode=light], :not(.dark,[data-a63-mode=dark]) > [data-a63-brand]...'; a cleaner one moves the mode choice into a --a63-mode-is-dark switch and declares the brand- and surface-derived tokens on ':root, [data-a63-brand], [data-a63-surface], [data-a63-mode], .light, .dark' using light-dark() or a 0/1 mix. Then add a nested brand-only and surface-only case to contrast.browser.test.ts and correct personalization-axes.md:71.
findings.verdictReason: Reproduced from the source. provider.tsx:68,73 stamps data-a63-brand or data-a63-surface alone, and data-a63-mode only when the mode prop is passed (:72). The only rules keyed on [data-a63-brand] are brand-ramp.css and brand-action.css:14-15. That file re-declares the action-primary set, --a63-brand-text and the gradients, but not --a63-focus-ring or --a63-text-accent. surface.css re-declares only --surface-light/dark-* and --a63-media-surface. Every semantic role that reads them sits only on ':root, .light, [data-a63-mode=light]' (semantics.css:95-97) and ':is(.dark,[data-a63-mode=dark])' (:306). That covers --a63-text-accent (:161 var(--a63-brand-text), :360), --a63-focus-ring (:209, :395), --a63-selected-accent-background (:301, :445), --a63-choice-card-checked-* (:199-205, :388-393) and every surface, text and border token. A custom property's var() resolves where it is declared, as the comment at brand-action.css:7-10 itself warns, so these roles inherit the root's values. A grep of packages/styles/src and packages/ui-react/src finds no other rule that re-declares them on [data-a63-brand] or [data-a63-surface]. A nested surface-only scope therefore changes nothing visible, and a nested brand-only scope changes only the primary fill. personalization-axes.md:4 says 'applied at any scope'. The agent-index personalization doc says 'A subtree can override one axis without resetting the others'. personalization-axes.md:71 wrongly puts --a63-focus-ring in tokens/brand.css on [data-a63-brand]. contrast.browser.test.ts:189-191 tests nesting only with theme and mode together. The brand tests set the brand only on the root (:233-237). P1 stands: UIProvider exposes the axis, the docs promise it works on a nested scope, and there it is mostly broken. One mitigation: a nested UIProvider that also passes mode works, because the mode selector re-resolves everything there.

findings.subject: Personalization axes (brand, surface, surface tint, radius, type scale, density, font, mode)
findings.summary: On a nested scope, the radius and type-scale axes do nothing, although the source comments say a subtree can override them.
findings.evidence: foundation/radius.css:16-32 and foundation/typography.css:18-49 declare the derived ramps at :root only; [data-a63-radius] and [data-a63-type-scale] change only the multiplier (radius.css:21-39, type-scale.css:12-26). radius.css:14 and type-scale.css:9-10 claim a subtree can reset them. story-probes.tsx:108-131 documents the freeze and re-emits the ramp inline as a workaround, and autocomplete.stories.tsx:220-235 ('Flush square items') sets data-a63-radius='none' on a wrapper that still draws var(--radius-lg) from the root. The test helpers set axes on documentElement only (test/apply-styles.ts:6-8).
findings.fix: Re-declare the --radius-* ramp on [data-a63-radius] and the --typography-* steps on [data-a63-type-scale] (as environment.css already does for density), move the story-probes workaround into the CSS, and add nested-scope cases to personalization-axes.browser.test.ts.

findings.subject: Theme: aqua
findings.summary: In a nested mode or theme-only scope, aqua loses its mode-split surfaces; terminal re-asserts its palette for descendants, but aqua does not.
findings.evidence: aqua.css:112 '[data-a63-theme=aqua]:is(:root,.light,[data-a63-mode=light])' and :134 '...:is(.dark,[data-a63-mode=dark])' have no descendant form, unlike terminal.css:94,152. A nested <UIProvider mode="dark"> re-runs semantics.css:306-326 and paints neutral modern-dark surfaces inside aqua. <UIProvider theme="aqua"> under an html-class mode matches neither rule.
findings.fix: Generate the descendant re-assertion for aqua (and modern.css:47) the same way as terminal: '[data-a63-theme=aqua] :is(.dark,[data-a63-mode=dark])', and a ':not(...)' or descendant light form. Add theme-only and nested-mode-inside-theme cases to the contrast test.

findings.subject: Theme: terminal
findings.summary: <UIProvider theme="terminal"> without a mode on the same element gets the CRT glow but neutral text and surfaces, and phosphor text ignores a nested brand.
findings.evidence: terminal.css:93-94 and 151-152 match only when the mode sits on the theme element or a descendant, never an ancestor (the next-themes html-class pattern). Phosphor text is color-mix(var(--a63-action-primary)) computed on the theme element (terminal.css:96-99, 154-158), so it freezes against a nested [data-a63-brand]. Not covered: contrast.browser.test.ts:189-191 always stamps theme and mode together.
findings.fix: Have UIProvider stamp the resolved mode whenever it stamps a theme, or add ':is(.dark,[data-a63-mode=dark]) [data-a63-theme=terminal]' ancestor forms. Declare the brand-derived phosphor tokens on [data-a63-brand] inside terminal too (same fix family as r2-tokens-1).

findings.subject: Foundation and semantic tokens (packages/styles/src/tokens)
findings.summary: --a63-status-*-foreground is not re-declared in the dark block, so a solid info or danger fill in a nested dark scope gets near-white text at 3.39:1 and 3.85:1. The pair is not declared in the contrast test.
findings.evidence: semantics.css:234-264 compute -foreground from var(--a63-status-*) in the light block only; the dark block :404-415 re-declares status-* and -subtle but not -foreground. Under a light root, -foreground keeps the step-600 result (white), while the nested fill is step 500: white on info-500 rgb(78,134,239) = 3.39:1, on danger-500 rgb(231,67,64) = 3.85:1. It reaches consumers as text-info-foreground (tailwind/theme.css:366) and --info-foreground (compat/shadcn.css:46). contrast.browser.test.ts:12-57 has no status-foreground-on-status-fill pair.
findings.fix: Re-declare the four -foreground tokens in the dark block (the generator already does this for -subtle), and add '{fg: --a63-status-X-foreground, bg: --a63-status-X, min: 4.5}' for each status to actionPairs, which also run nested.

findings.subject: Foundation and semantic tokens (packages/styles/src/tokens)
findings.summary: Chart series 2 and 3 are under 3:1 against the light page, and no chart or category pair is declared.
findings.evidence: semantics.css:270-271 set --a63-chart-2 to teal-500 and --a63-chart-3 to amber-500 on light surfaces (palette.css:43,98). Against the n1 light page rgb(249,249,249), teal-500 is about 2.3:1 and amber-500 about 2.0:1 (computed from the sRGB equivalents). The same 500 steps feed --a63-category-* (semantics.css:49-92), which AGENTS.md rule 9 steers chart series to. contrast.browser.test.ts declares no chart or category pair.
findings.fix: Either move the light-mode chart and category hues to step 600 or 700 where needed to reach 3:1 against the page and panel, and declare them as AA_UI pairs, or document that series need a direct label or outline (and enforce that in the chart recipe). Product direction on palette brightness may need YZ.

findings.subject: Foundation and semantic tokens (packages/styles/src/tokens)
findings.summary: Dead tokens are not checked. The token-economy unused scan only covers prefixes that no longer exist, and 60 --a63-* tokens in packages/styles have no reader in the repo.
findings.evidence: check-token-economy.mjs:42-46 filters with /^--(theme|gel)-/; there are 0 such declarations in packages/styles/src, so the log always says '0 unused'. A multiline-aware scan of packages/ and apps/ finds 60 unread --a63-* tokens, including 40 --a63-badge-<hue>-accent/-foreground (contracts/badge.css:10-53; the Badge recipe reads --badge-bg/--badge-fg), --a63-status-danger-subtle(-foreground) (semantics.css:265-266), --a63-choice-thumb, --a63-choice-feedback-duration, --a63-toggle-group-gap, --a63-toggle-shadow-active, --a63-trigger-indicator-size, --a63-action-control-gap, and the weather border, divider, muted-foreground and text-shadow tokens that three themes set (aqua.css, retro.css, terminal.css) but no web recipe reads.
findings.fix: Scan --a63-* and the theme-private prefixes in use (--aqua-, --retro-, --terminal-) for unused tokens, fail on new ones against a baseline, then delete or wire up the listed tokens. If the weather tokens serve an app outside this repo, say so in the contract.

findings.subject: Foundation and semantic tokens (packages/styles/src/tokens)
findings.summary: The type scale is not monotonic: 10xl (the display role) is a fixed 40px, below 9xl's 44px at 640px and 49px at 768px. The steps around it are a 1px step and then a 1.4x jump.
findings.evidence: foundation/typography.css:47-48 (10xl 40/44, 11xl 56/60, with no breakpoint override) against :53-98 (9xl 44px at >=40rem, 49px at >=48rem). type-roles.css:27 maps --a63-type-display-font-size to 10xl, so 'display' renders smaller than the 9xl step on tablet and desktop. At the base width, 9xl to 10xl is 39 to 40px.

findings.subject: Tailwind bridge (packages/styles/src/tailwind)

Templates lay out with utilities such as 'flex flex-col gap-6 p-6' (app-view template), and the template description tells builders to use <UIProvider density="compact"> for dense views.
findings.fix: Map Tailwind's --spacing to var(--a63-space-unit) in @theme inline (or document that layout utilities are density-invariant and give templates density-aware gap tokens). Check that the change is intended across the templates' visual baselines.

findings.subject: Tailwind bridge (packages/styles/src/tailwind)
findings.summary: The bridge keeps Tailwind's names with other values: text-6xl is 28px rather than 60px, text-9xl is 39-49px, and rounded-full (a pill) and --radius-full (a 28px corner) are one name with two meanings.
findings.evidence: foundation/typography.css:39,45 (6xl 28px, 9xl 39px) exposed as --text-6xl/--text-9xl in tailwind/theme.css; theme.css:517-519 maps rounded-full to --radius-pill while foundation/radius.css:32 keeps --radius-full = 2 x xl. A builder or agent fluent in Tailwind gets a different result for the same class.
findings.fix: Decide between keeping Tailwind's numeric meaning (and moving the DS ramp to role utilities such as text-title-1, which type-roles already provides) and documenting the remap prominently in atom63 rules and docs. Rename --radius-full (for example --radius-soft) so that 'full' means a pill everywhere.

findings.subject: Theme: terminal
findings.summary: In Figma, terminal's brand-tracking phosphor colors always show the b1 value, and the parity test leaves these 'computed' tokens out.

findings.fix: Emit terminal's brand-derived colors as a Theme x Brand product collection (or per-brand terminal modes) in generate-figma-sync.mjs, or alias them to Brand-collection variables so that switching the Brand mode re-tints them. Then drop them from 'computed'.

findings.subject: Figma sync and parity (generated/atom63.figma-sync.json)
findings.summary: Figma has no phone form-factor, compact-density control geometry or coarse-pointer sizes, so designs drawn for those contexts use comfortable desktop values.
findings.evidence: Model 'skipped' tally: 60 "context scope: [data-a63-form-factor='phone']...", 32 ':is([data-a63-density], [data-density])', 53 'conditional' (@media pointer: coarse, prefers-reduced-motion, max-width). --a63-control-height-xs..xl are in 'computed'. The Density collection holds only the --a63-space-* steps.
findings.fix: Add a Form Factor collection (desktop, phone) and move the density-scoped control tokens into the Density collection as concrete per-mode values (the generator already resolves values per context in the browser). Keep 'conditional' tokens out only where Figma has no equivalent.

findings.subject: Personalization axes (brand, surface, surface tint, radius, type scale, density, font, mode)
findings.summary: UIProvider mode="system" stamps light whatever the OS preference, so 'system', a documented value of the mode axis, never resolves to dark on a nested scope.
findings.evidence: ui-react/src/provider.tsx:65 'const resolvedMode = mode === 'system' ? 'light' : mode', stamped at :72. personalization-axes.md:22 lists system as a mode value. applyPersonalization resolves system with matchMedia (apply-personalization.ts:3-14), so the two stamping paths disagree.
findings.fix: Resolve 'system' in UIProvider with useSyncExternalStore over matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)') (light on the server), or leave data-a63-mode unset and add a prefers-color-scheme fallback block in semantics.css.

findings.subject: button
findings.summary: Button contract slots are wrong: none of root/label/icon/spinner/indicator is a rendered data-slot. The CLI serves them to agents next to the true data-slot="button".
findings.evidence: packages/ui-foundation/contracts/components/button.json:42 vs packages/ui-react/src/components/button/button.tsx:72,76,83,99; `pnpm -s atom63 component button` lines 30 and 167 contradict each other.
findings.fix: Set slots to ["button","button-label","button-spinner","button-indicator"] (drop "icon" or render it), regenerate contracts, and add a test that every contract slot occurs as a data-slot in the component source.
findings.verdictReason: Reproduced. button.json:42 lists slots [root,label,icon,spinner,indicator], but button.tsx renders data-slot="button" (99), "button-label" (72), "button-spinner" (76), "button-indicator" (83), and nothing renders an icon slot. Every other contract uses the full data-slot names (alert.json:8 [alert, alert-icon, ...], badge.json:71 [badge, badge-dot], button-group.json:14), so Button is the odd one out, not following some other convention. `pnpm -s atom63 component button` prints data-slot="button" in its metadata table and then `Slots: root, label, icon, spinner, indicator`, so an agent that writes [data-slot="label"] or [data-slot="icon"] matches nothing. P1 is fair: it is wrong metadata on the most-used component, but rendering is not affected.

findings.subject: @atom63/ui-react
findings.summary: The @atom63/ui-react root entry does not tree-shake. One small component costs 36-110 kB gzip, and the size check cannot see it.
findings.evidence: esbuild 0.28.2 one-symbol probes against packages/ui-react/dist/index.js (minified ESM, react external): Kbd 36,509 B gzip, Badge 38,247, Button 38,759, Separator 109,752. Every probe retains all of @atom63/ui-foundation (72.2 kB min), tailwind-merge (27.5 kB), sonner (19.7 kB) and input-otp (9.6 kB); Separator also retains 178.8 kB of @base-ui/react. Causes in dist/index.js (5535 lines, one module): static `import ... from 'sonner'` (:23-24) and `'input-otp'` (:29) evaluated for every consumer, and un-annotated top-level calls that bundlers must keep: React3.createContext at :42, :43, :485, :1262, :1924, :2610, :2760, :2788, :4105, :5023, :5163, :5463, and `getCrossRendererContract("load-more-trigger")` at :3069, which drags in the full cross-renderer contract table. check:ui-react-size (check-ui-react-bundle-size.mjs:117-139) only sums gzip of every dist chunk (97.3/100 kB) and has been raised 13 times since 64 kB (:9-116); check:ui-react-root-deps guards only react-day-picker. Downstream: mdx credits-block 164 kB and widgets ./state 167 kB (r2-architecture-2, -3).
findings.fix: Build per-component modules (tsup/rollup preserveModules, or one entry per component folder re-exported by the root) so an unused component's imports are never evaluated. Mark top-level createContext/forwardRef/memo calls /* @__PURE__ */ (or move getCrossRendererContract lookups inside the component). Replace or add to the total-size budget an import-cost check (size-limit or an esbuild probe like the one above) for representative single imports, e.g. Button <= 8 kB gzip, failing in CI.
findings.verdictReason: Reproduced with node_modules/.pnpm/esbuild@0.28.2 (one-symbol import of packages/ui-react/dist/index.js, --bundle --minify --format=esm, react/react-dom/jsx-runtime external): Kbd 36,462 B gzip, Badge 38,197, Button 38,709, Separator 109,707. The Kbd metafile keeps ui-foundation/dist/index.js 72,219 B, tailwind-merge 27,458, sonner 19,659 and input-otp 9,567. dist/index.js:23-24 imports sonner (and re-exports toast), :29 imports input-otp, and :42/:43/:485/:1262/:1924/:2610/:2760/:2788/:4105/:5023/:5163/:5463 call React3.createContext at top level with no annotation. :3069 calls getCrossRendererContract("load-more-trigger") at top level, so ui-foundation's sideEffects:false does not help. ui-react's package.json sideEffects lists only CSS, but the root is one 5535-line module, so that cannot help either. check-ui-react-bundle-size.mjs:117-139 only sums the gzip of all dist .js files against a 100 kB budget, and the comments above it record the repeated raises. The bar's criterion A2 is literally 'Entries tree-shake' (proposal-ds-review-bar.md:103), so this is a gap that blocks 'ready', not inflated. P1 stands.

findings.subject: AGENTS.md rules vs checks
findings.summary: 7 of the 15 AGENTS.md rules (1 query-first, 2 compose-before-create, 3 contract-values, 6 quiet-secondary-actions, 7 one-boundary, 8 on-media-colors, 14 as-child-spreads-props) name no enforcing check and give no reason why not, and check:agents-md only verifies the block is in sync, so nothing holds the bar's U2 criterion.
findings.evidence: AGENTS.md:76-90; packages/cli/src/rules.mjs:19,35,40,45,80 (no `check` field); packages/cli/scripts/sync-agents-md.mjs:18-26 (diff only). check:craft `token-role` has no matching rule. Repo-level rules (changeset per published-package change, no brand icons in ui-react) have no CI gate.
findings.fix: Give every rule in rules.mjs either `check` or `unchecked: '<why>'` (e.g. contract-values: TypeScript unions reject other values; query-first: process rule, not checkable), render the reason in the generated block, and make check:agents-md fail on a rule with neither. Add a token-role rule (or fold it into rule 4's wording). Where cheap, add vibe-measure/craft lint for rule 6 (ghost without tone="muted" in toolbars) and rule 8.
findings.verdictReason: Core claim reproduced. packages/cli/src/rules.mjs: query-first, compose-before-create, contract-values, quiet-secondary-actions, one-boundary, on-media-colors and as-child-spreads-props have no `check` field, and their `why` text gives no reason they are unchecked. accent-sparingly and accessible-by-default also lack `check`, but their text points to the vibe measures and axe, so they are excluded fairly. packages/cli/src/agents-md.mjs:46-54 adds an enforcement sentence only when `check` is set, so it never writes a 'why not'. packages/cli/scripts/sync-agents-md.mjs:18-24 only compares the generated block with the file. The bar (proposal-ds-review-bar.md:114) makes U2 'enforced by a check, or says why not' with `check:agents-md` as its gate, so U2 is unmet and that blocks 'ready' (P1). token-role is a real check:craft rule (scripts/design-system/lib/craft-rules.test.mjs:252) with no matching AGENTS rule. Two caveats. First, the side claim that the changeset rule has no CI gate is wrong: .github/workflows/ci.yml:234-241 runs `pnpm changeset status --since=origin/<base>` on pull requests. Second, I found no gate for 'no brand icons in ui-react' (AGENTS.md:51). The fix is mostly writing reasons, so it is cheap, but the criterion is unmet as written.

findings.subject: popover
findings.summary: PopoverAnchor is a stable export that renders an unwired <div>; it never anchors the popup.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/popover/popover.tsx:100-107; Base UI Popover has no Anchor part and PopoverContent never passes `anchor` to the Positioner (popover.tsx:81-87); popover.test.tsx:53-65 only checks data-slot.

findings.verdictReason: Real: popover.tsx:100-107 renders a bare div with data-slot and className only, PopoverContent (66-98) never passes `anchor` to PopoverPrimitive.Positioner, and popover.test.tsx:53-65 only checks the data-slot. The agent-index docs even promise 'a trigger or custom anchor'. Severity is inflated, though. Popover itself works and anchors to the trigger. Only the compatibility part is a no-op, and nothing in the repo uses it. That makes it a gap a consumer can hit (P2), the same severity round 1 gave this exact finding (readiness-r1/register.json:1818, grouped under the 'API leftovers' P2s). It does not block 'ready'.

The claim that 'none of the four tones is ever captured' overstates it: ui-react-toaster-scoped-dark-region-chromium-linux.png captures a default-variant success toast (toaster.stories.tsx:62), and the Inverse baseline captures loading. findings.subject: toaster
findings.summary: The default toast ignores the overlay archetype tokens, so it looks the same flat card in every theme, and there is no Themes matrix.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/toaster/toaster.tsx:31-37 sets only --normal-bg/border/text and --radius-lg; other overlays read --a63-overlay-shadow/-gloss/-texture/-inner-shadow/-backdrop/-radius (popover.css:25-31). toaster.stories.tsx:54 notes there is no Themes matrix.
findings.fix: Map the overlay contract onto the Sonner toast (shadow, gloss/texture background-image, backdrop, var(--a63-overlay-radius, var(--radius-lg))) in toaster.css and add a Themes story with raised toasts. Taste is provisional pending YZ.
findings.verdictReason: Confirmed that toaster.tsx:31-37 sets only --border-radius, --normal-bg, --normal-border and --normal-text, with no --a63-overlay-shadow/-gloss/-texture/-backdrop, unlike popover.css:25-31. There is no Themes story (toaster.stories.tsx:54-55). The premise that it 'ignores the overlay archetype' does not match the contract, though: toaster.json lists visualArchetypes ['surface'], not 'overlay'. So this is a contract/recipe mismatch (the contract arguably mislabels a floating toast), not a recipe that ignores its declared archetype. Also, 'looks the same in every theme' is overstated, because bg, border, text and radius come from theme tokens (--a63-surface-overlay, --radius-lg) and so vary by theme. K3 is taste and provisional pending YZ. Overall a P2 consistency gap.

findings.verdictReason: Real but overstated. Confirmed in source: card.css:67-85 gives interactive/overlay cursor:pointer and a hover lift, and there is no .a63-Card:focus-visible rule; the only focus ring is .a63-CardLink:focus-visible (card.css:343). card.stories.tsx Compositions (the second interactive card, about line 204, with only a Kbd arrow) and CursorLabel/LinkCard (lines 270-290) are div cards with no anchor, and `pnpm -s atom63 example card` serves these stories. findings.subject: text-ticker

findings.verdictReason: text-ticker.tsx:23/39/107/113: autoPlay sets data-autoplay once the text overflows. text-ticker.css:101-107 then runs the track animation 'infinite', and the same rule animates on :hover/:focus-within, so hovering doesn't pause it. The component has no pause control or play-state hook, which fails WCAG 2.2.2 (only prefers-reduced-motion stops it, :118-125). Marquee solves the same rule with a built-in toggle (marquee.tsx:35-37, 86-97). The prop is opt-in (default false), but whenever it is used it is inaccessible, and a consumer has no way to fix that through the component, so P1 stands.

findings.subject: load-more-trigger
findings.summary: In dark mode the failed-state Retry label (and its icon) is drawn in --a63-action-danger, which stays danger-600 in dark and gives about 2.8-2.95:1 on dark surfaces, below the 4.5:1 WCAG 1.4.3 needs for text.
findings.evidence: load-more-trigger.css:28-30 sets --load-more-accent: var(--a63-action-danger) for data-tone=error; css:93 paints .a63-LoadMoreTrigger-action with it. packages/styles/src/tokens/semantics.css:215 (action-danger = danger-600, no dark override; comment :255-258 says error text uses --a63-text-danger, which moves to danger-400 at :363). danger-600 rgb(187,29,34) vs n1-dark-1 rgb(17,17,17) = 2.95:1, vs n1-dark-2 rgb(25,25,25) = 2.78:1 (computed from primitives.css:95,123-124). findings.verdictReason: Reproduced from source. load-more-trigger.tsx:124-131 renders the Retry <button> inside the data-tone=error row. load-more-trigger.css:28-30 sets --load-more-accent to var(--a63-action-danger), and css:93 (label) and css:79 (AlertCircle icon) paint with it. In semantics.css, action-danger is danger-600 at :215, and the dark block (~:396-400) overrides only -hover/-subtle/-subtle-foreground, never the base. So dark stays rgba(187,29,34) (foundation/primitives.css:95; the finding's primitives.css path is off by one directory). The dark block's own comment at semantics.css:361-362 says step 600 is 'about 2.7:1' on dark surfaces and moves --a63-text-danger to danger-400 for that reason. The Retry text therefore fails 4.5:1, and the icon also misses 3:1. --a63-status-danger moves to 500 in dark (:413), but this component does not use it. The failed message span itself uses text-secondary (css:47), so only the Retry label and icon are affected. P1 holds.

findings.subject: chat-composer
findings.summary: The inline layout only detects wrapping inside onChange, so long text that arrives by prefill, a long defaultValue without a newline, or a narrower container stays in the radius-full pill while it wraps.

findings.subject: @atom63/inform InformSpotlight
findings.summary: In forced-colors mode the spotlight draws neither its scrim nor its cutout, so it no longer shows which control it is about.
findings.evidence: packages/inform/src/surfaces/inform-spotlight.css:19-23 draws both with `box-shadow: 0 0 0 9999px var(--a63-scrim)`; forced colors drop box-shadow; `grep -rn forced-colors packages/inform/src` returns nothing. No ForcedColors story (visual.setup.ts captures `--forced-colors` stories, none in inform).
findings.fix: Add `@media (forced-colors: active)` for the cutout: an `outline: 3px solid Highlight` (or CanvasText) around the anchor rect, and optionally a Canvas-coloured translucent backdrop; add a `ForcedColors` story so visual.setup.ts captures it.
findings.verdictReason: The gap is real. packages/inform/src/surfaces/inform-spotlight.css:19-24 draws the scrim and the hole with only `box-shadow: 0 0 0 9999px var(--a63-scrim)`, which forced colors drops. `grep -rln forced-colors packages` finds no hit under packages/inform, and no inform story has a forced-colors variant. But the claim that it 'no longer shows which control it is about' goes too far. The bubble (.a63-InformSpotlight-bubble, lines 26-40) keeps a real border (--a63-overlay-border-width), so it still shows in forced colors. It is still placed beside the anchor from the anchor's rect (place-bubble.ts). It is still a labelled modal dialog (inform-spotlight.tsx:207-220, role=dialog, aria-modal, aria-labelledby/-describedby). Forced-colors users lose the highlight and the page dimming, but they still get the guide step next to its control. That is a gap a consumer can hit, not one that blocks 'ready', so P2. The fix is small: a forced-colors outline on the cutout, e.g. `outline: 2px solid Highlight`.

findings.subject: All subjects in @atom63/mdx, @atom63/inform, @atom63/widgets, @atom63/brand

findings.subject: @atom63/inform surfaces and @atom63/widgets components
findings.summary: `atom63 api` answers for inform surfaces and widget components give only an import line and a docs link (no props, no example), and `atom63 component`/`atom63 example` know none of the four packages.
findings.evidence: Loop over `pnpm -s atom63 api <name>`: MDX blocks return 2-18 props and an example; InformBanner, InformDialog, InformCornerFlyout, InformSpotlight, WidgetCard, WidgetSurface, WidgetAvatar, WidgetStateFeedback, WidgetHostedShell, WidgetImage return 0 props. `atom63 component inform-banner` and `atom63 example image-compare` return component.not_found. pattern-inform lists no surface props.

findings.subject: @atom63/mdx blocks (Callout, ColorSwatchItem, Compare, ComparisonPair, CreditsBlock, DocExample, DocExampleCode, ExampleContainer, FigureBlock, KeyIdea, LayerStack, MdxPageSkeleton, MediaCaption, MediaPlaceholder, MermaidDiagram, PageMeta, PageTableOfContents, ResourceList, ScrollStage, StatCard, StatGrid, Steps, Timeline, VideoBlock)
findings.summary: Most MDX blocks drop unknown props and refs: an author's id, aria-*, data-* or ref never reaches the DOM.
findings.evidence: Survey of packages/mdx/src/blocks/*/*.tsx: only accordion, code-block, image-compare and tabs spread rest props; only image-compare and demo-stage forward a ref. e.g. callout.tsx:19 `function Callout({ children, type = 'info', className })`; MermaidDiagram takes no className at all (mermaid-diagram.tsx:35-41).
findings.fix: Type each block's props as its root element's ComponentProps plus its own, spread the rest onto the root, and accept ref (React 19 ref-as-prop).

findings.subject: @atom63/inform InformBanner, InformDialog, InformCornerFlyout, InformFlyoutStack, InformSpotlight
findings.summary: Inform surfaces accept a closed prop set: no rest props and no ref, so consumers cannot add an id, data-* or aria attributes, or pass an element instead of a selector to the spotlight.
findings.evidence: packages/inform/src/surfaces/types.ts:9-34 (InformSurfaceProps), flyout-stack.tsx:8-14, inform-spotlight.tsx:16-20 (anchor: string).
findings.fix: Extend the surface props with the root element's HTML attributes, spread them on the root, accept ref; let `anchor` also take an Element or RefObject.

findings.subject: @atom63/widgets WidgetCard parts, WidgetAvatar, WidgetStateFeedback, WidgetImage
findings.summary: Widget card parts and the memo components take only children/className, so ids, aria-* and refs are dropped; WidgetImageProps is not exported.
findings.evidence: packages/widgets/src/primitives/widget-card.tsx:70-255 (Header, HeaderLeft, HeaderRight, Content, Block, Block regions, Title, TextGroup, Row); widget-avatar.tsx:37-48; widget-state-feedback.tsx:128-129; widgets.api.md:185 ae-forgotten-export WidgetImageProps.
findings.fix: Spread rest props and accept ref on every part (as WidgetCard and WidgetSurface already do), and export WidgetImageProps.

findings.subject: @atom63/inform InformBanner, InformCornerFlyout, InformSpotlight
findings.summary: The inform dismiss control's hit area is 24px on every pointer; it never grows to 44px on touch.
findings.evidence: packages/inform/src/surfaces/inform-parts.css:57-61 `.a63-InformDismissButton::after { inset: calc((1lh - 1.5rem) / 2) }`; dismiss-button.tsx:17 comment '24px WCAG target'; `grep -rn coarse packages/inform/src` returns nothing.
findings.fix: Add `@media (pointer: coarse) { .a63-InformDismissButton::after { inset: calc((1lh - 2.75rem) / 2) } }` (or read the system's coarse target token), keeping the one-line layout box.

findings.subject: @atom63/mdx ImageCompare
findings.summary: ImageCompare's slider is named with the library's fixed English instruction, not the before/after labels, and authors cannot translate it.
findings.evidence: react-compare-slider@4.0.0 dist sets aria-label 'Click and drag or focus and use arrow keys to change the position of the slider'; ImageCompare passes no name (packages/mdx/src/blocks/image-compare/image-compare.tsx:266-277).

findings.subject: @atom63/inform InformDialog
findings.summary: InformDialog ignores `dismissLabel`, and its close button's name is a hard-coded English 'Close', so the dialog is the one inform surface whose dismiss control cannot be translated.
findings.evidence: packages/inform/src/surfaces/inform-dialog.tsx:30-41 omits dismissLabel; packages/ui-react/src/components/dialog/dialog.tsx:163 `aria-label="Close"`.
findings.fix: Add a close-label prop to ui-react DialogPopup and pass dismissLabel through from InformDialog; add a test.

findings.subject: @atom63/inform InformCornerFlyout (InformFlyoutStack)
findings.summary: The flyout stack is placed a fixed space-4 from the corner and ignores safe-area insets, so on notched or home-indicator phones a card can sit under system UI.
findings.evidence: packages/inform/src/surfaces/inform-corner-flyout.css:56-61 (right/left: var(--a63-space-4)); offsets along the anchored edge come from the `offset` prop (flyout-stack.tsx:13); `grep -rn safe-area packages/inform/src` returns nothing; no flyout phone story.
findings.fix: Add env(safe-area-inset-*) to the stack's side and anchored-edge offsets (max(offset, inset)), and a Phone story.

findings.subject: @atom63/widgets WidgetAvatar
findings.summary: Pressing shuffle from the keyboard disables the focused button, which drops focus to the page, and the busy state is not announced.
findings.evidence: packages/widgets/src/primitives/widget-avatar.tsx:72-77 `<button … disabled={busy}>`; no aria-busy or live text in the component.
findings.fix: Use aria-disabled with a guarded onClick instead of disabled while busy, keep focus on the button, and expose aria-busy (or a polite status) during the shuffle.

findings.subject: @atom63/widgets WidgetAvatar
findings.summary: On touch screens the shuffle affordance is invisible: it shows only on hover, keyboard focus or while busy, and its target is not lifted to 44px.
findings.evidence: packages/widgets/src/primitives/widget-avatar.css:88 (opacity: 0), :98-100 (busy, focus-visible), :115-118 (@media (hover: hover)); the coarse 44px rule targets only .a63-Button (packages/widgets/src/layout/widget-layout.css:26-38) and shuffle is a raw <button> (widget-avatar.tsx:72).
findings.fix: Under (hover: none) show a persistent small shuffle badge (or rest the glyph at partial opacity), and include .a63-WidgetAvatar-shuffle in the coarse target rule.

findings.subject: @atom63/mdx ResourceList
findings.summary: ResourceList's row divider is positioned with physical left/right, so in RTL it is inset from the wrong side; check:craft does not catch it because left/right positioning is out of the rule's scope.

findings.subject: @atom63/mdx DocExample
findings.summary: DocExample sizes its tabs and copy button by viewport width, not pointer: at 768px and up a touch device gets 28px targets, and the copy button overrides the ui-react size with custom classes.

findings.subject: @atom63/mdx Callout; @atom63/inform surfaces; ui-react Alert
